2607.06163.title: X-FEMR: A Token-level Explainable Approach for Electronic Health Records Foundation Models using Transformer-based Models
2607.06163.paper_summary: Foundation Models for Electronic Health Records (FEMRs) are pretrained on large-scale structured patient data, enabling them to convert longitudinal patient trajectories into generalizable representations for diverse clinical prediction tasks. Despite their effectiveness, FEMRs remain black-box models, raising concerns about bias, interpretability, and clinical trust. To address this, we propose the first token-level explainability approach for FEMRs. We train a Transformer-based surrogate model on input-output pairs from the FEMR across two prediction tasks, approximating its behavior while preserving temporal dynamics. We identify the most influential tokens, providing insights into how FEMRs leverage different aspects of patient history for predictions. To evaluate clinical relevance, we introduce a novel clinical alignment metric that quantifies the correspondence between the surrogate model's key tokens and clinically validated features. Our results demonstrate that the surrogate closely approximates FEMR predictions and that token-level explanations align well with clinical knowledge, offering a practical framework for interpretable and trustworthy clinical AI.
2607.06163.paper_summary_zh: 基於電子健康紀錄的基礎模型（FEMRs）在大規模結構化患者數據上進行預訓練，使其能夠將縱向患者軌跡轉換為可泛化的表示，以應對多樣的臨床預測任務。儘管其有效性，FEMRs 仍然是黑箱模型，這引發了對偏見、可解釋性和臨床信任的擔憂。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了第一個針對 FEMRs 的標記級解釋方法。我們在來自 FEMR 的輸入-輸出對上訓練了一個基於 Transformer 的替代模型，近似其行為，同時保留時間動態。我們識別出最具影響力的標記，提供了對 FEMRs 如何利用患者歷史的不同方面進行預測的見解。為了評估臨床相關性，我們引入了一個新穎的臨床對齊度量，量化替代模型的關鍵標記與臨床驗證特徵之間的對應關係。我們的結果顯示，替代模型與 FEMR 預測之間的近似度很高，且標記級解釋與臨床知識良好對齊，提供了一個可解釋且值得信賴的臨床 AI 實用框架。
